malik:471|471|15|2.text: Yahya related to me from Malik, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that Umar ibn al-Khattab was with a group of people who were reciting the Qur’an. He went to relieve himself, then returned while reciting the Qur’an. A man said to him, ‘Commander of the Faithful, are you reciting the Qur’an when you do not have wudu?’ Umar said to him, ‘Who gave you that ruling—Musaylimah?’

malik:486|486|15|17.text: Yahya related to me from Malik, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Sa‘sa‘ah, from his father, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that he heard a man reciting ‘Say: He is Allah, One,’ repeating it. In the morning he went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned this to him, as though the man considered it little. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed equivalent to one third of the Qur’an.’

malik:523|523|16|4.text: Yahya related to me from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was shrouded in three white Sahuli cloths, with neither a shirt nor a turban among them.

malik:672|672|18|43.text: Malik said, ‘A similar report has reached me from Sulayman ibn Yasar.’ Malik said, ‘If someone dies owing a vow to free an enslaved person, to fast, to give charity, or to offer a sacrificial camel, and leaves instructions that it be fulfilled on his behalf from his property, then the charity and the sacrificial camel are to come from the one third of his estate available for bequests. This takes priority over other bequests, except those of the same kind. That is because obligations owed through vows and the like are not the same as voluntary acts that are not obligatory. This is assigned specifically to his one third, rather than to the estate as a whole. If it were permissible to take it from the estate as a whole, the deceased could postpone such obligations until death approached and the property was passing to his heirs, and then name obligations of this sort that no claimant had been demanding from him. If that were permissible, he could delay these matters until his death, then specify them, and they might consume all his property. He is not entitled to do that.’
malik:672|672|18|43.note: This source entry begins by referring to an earlier report. Its opening ‘a similar report’ is retained without reconstructing the missing context. This is a translation of Malik’s statement, not personal legal guidance.

malik:695|695|19|6.text: Ziyad related to me from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman, from Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intended to observe i‘tikaf. When he went to the place where he intended to stay in retreat, he found tents: Aishah’s tent, Hafsah’s tent, and Zaynab’s tent. When he saw them, he asked about them and was told, ‘These are the tents of Aishah, Hafsah, and Zaynab.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Do you regard these as acts of piety?’ Then he left and did not observe i‘tikaf until he spent ten days in retreat in Shawwal.

malik:995|995|21|37.text: Yahya related to me from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to provide transport on forty thousand camels in a single year. He would assign one camel to a man going to Syria, and one camel to two men going to Iraq. A man from Iraq came to him and said, ‘Provide a mount for me and Suhaym.’ Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him, ‘I ask you by Allah: is Suhaym a skin bag?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’
malik:995|995|21|37.note: The Arabic calls Suhaym a ziqq, a skin bag or container. This translation does not infer its contents.

malik:1055|1055|25|4.text: Yahya also related to me from Malik, from Nafi‘, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, that he used to say concerning a trained hunting dog, ‘Eat whatever it catches for you, whether it has killed it or not.’

malik:1058|1058|25|7.text: Yahya also related to me from Malik, from Nafi‘, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah asked Abd Allah ibn Umar about what the sea had cast ashore, and he forbade him to eat it. Nafi‘ said: Then Abd Allah returned and asked for the written Qur’an. He read, ‘Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food.’ Nafi‘ said: Abd Allah ibn Umar then sent me to Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah to tell him that there was no harm in eating it.

malik:1390|1390|34|1.text: Yahya related to us from Malik, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, from Hanzalah ibn Qays al-Zuraqi, from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prohibited renting farmland. Hanzalah said: I asked Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, ‘For gold and silver?’ He replied, ‘As for gold and silver, there is no harm in that.’

malik:1598|1598|45|1.text: Yahya ibn Yahya related to me, saying: Malik related to me from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘O Allah, bless their measure for them, and bless their sa‘ and their mudd for them,’ meaning the people of Madinah.
malik:1598|1598|45|1.note: Sa‘ and mudd are traditional measures of capacity; no modern-unit conversion has been added.

malik:1763|1763|54|1.text: Malik related to me from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata ibn Yasar, that a man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ‘Messenger of Allah, should I ask permission before entering upon my mother?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ The man said, ‘I live with her in the house.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Ask her permission.’ The man said, ‘I look after her.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Ask her permission. Would you like to see her naked?’ He said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Then ask her permission.’
